subject: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jen Morris <jen.morris@atlasretail.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy

Team —

Atlas Retail (DEAL-4832) plans to upgrade to model v13 for their recommendation pipeline on Wed 18 Mar. They want a progressive canary (A/B) rollout to validate latency and quality in production. Given the size of their traffic and the potential P95 latency delta during warmups, I'm requesting a temporary SLA exception and approval for the following guardrails to mitigate risk: 

- Rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 checkpoints; each checkpoint is 30 minutes of golden-signal observation (metrics below).
- Automatic fallback: if P95 latency for the canary slice > 800ms OR error rate increase > 0.5% for two consecutive windows, route all canary traffic back to pinned stable model (stable-v12) automatically.
- Pinning: hold stable-v12 pinned as the fallback variant; do not garbage-collect or auto-upgrade it during the exception window.
- Monitoring & alerts: enable token-level latency traces and webhook to Atlas on critical rollback; set SLO window to 1h for decisioning.
- Exception window: request approval for a 48-hour exception starting 2026-03-18T01:00:00Z to allow one full canary run and any necessary follow-ups.

Attached: canary_runbook_v2.pdf and draft SLA exception form (sla_exception_request_AtlasRetail.docx). Please reply with approvals, technical sign-off, and the customer-facing rollback contact.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Lead, GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jen Morris <jen.morris@atlasretail.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy

Laura —

Thumbs up on the guardrails. Two asks from sales/AM side before I externalize the dates to Atlas: 

1) Add a short customer-facing blurb that says: "We will fallback to the previously pinned model automatically if latency or error thresholds are violated; there will be no data retention or schema change impacting your telemetry."
2) Provide an expected cost delta for the 48-hour exception (approx GPU-hours / estimated token volume) so procurement knows the impact.

If we have both, I can confirm the start time to Jen and coordinate the calendar invite and post-deploy review.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jen Morris <jen.morris@atlasretail.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy

Laura / team —

Engineering sign-off with a few implementation notes: 

- We will implement the canary policy via the routing layer using route.policy=canary with a fallback key pinned to stable-v12. The pin will be enforced at the routing table level and will ignore auto-update jobs while pinned.
- Rollout windows: prefer 1-hour observation windows for real traffic at the 25% and 50% steps; 30 minutes is OK for the initial 5% warmup but the 25% step should be longer to capture tail behaviour.
- Auto-rollback triggers: P95 > 800ms OR 2x baseline CPU or error-rate delta > 0.5%. The action will be an atomic route swap to the pinned stable variant and a throttled alert to on-call (pager).
- Metric hooks: we'll emit canary.variant P50/P95, infra CPU, queue latencies, and a synthetic check from the EU region. Console dashboards will be shared.

I've attached the runbook excerpt to the canary_runbook_v2.pdf (pages 3–6). Ops will implement the pin for the exception window and coordinate with SRE to ensure no GC or rolling compaction occurs on the pinned model.

Grace O'Connor
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Jen Morris <jen.morris@atlasretail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy

Thanks Laura —

Appreciate the detail. A couple of things from our security/procurement side: 

- Please confirm no change to data retention, and that the automatic fallback does not copy or export customer telemetry outside our configured region.
- Who is the on-call contact we should reach if rollback is triggered? We need a response SLA from that person (30 minutes preferred).

If those are covered, we are happy to proceed with the 48-hour window.

Regards,
Jen Morris
Head of Engineering — Data Platforms
Atlas Retail
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: rollout guardrails & temporary SLA exception for Canary A/B policy

All —

Finalizing approvals:

- Confirmed: no data retention changes or cross-region exports during the canary; fallback does not create additional copies of telemetry. (Grace confirmed routing-only swap.)
- On-call: Vivek Kulkarni will be primary pager for rollback; he accepts a 30-minute acknowledgement SLA for this window.
- Cost impact: Aditya — can you send the quick estimate by EOD so procurement has the figure?
- Exception approved for 48 hours starting 2026-03-18T01:00:00Z. Ops will pin stable-v12 at 00:45Z and open the exception form in the record.

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9123 (canary job), HubSpot DEAL-4832.

Thanks everyone — proceeding to notify Atlas and schedule the kickoff.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Lead, GTM
Redwood Inference
